summary: Extends the snoop packet capture file format with identifiers for additional link-layer media types. The snoop format stores network packet traces so they can be saved and exchanged between tools, and this memo adds codes for newer kinds of network links.

plainLanguage.summary: A photo album for network traffic has labels for each kind of cable. This document adds more labels for new kinds.

questions: what is the snoop file format
subtitle: Adds Fibre Channel, ATM and InfiniBand codes to the snoop packet capture file format and creates an IANA registry.

tldr.problem: The snoop capture file format identifies the network type with a Datalink Type field, but needed values for newer media.
tldr.mechanism: The memo defines codes 16 (Fibre Channel), 17 (ATM), 18 (ATM Classical IP) and 26 (IP over Infiniband), and creates the IANA registry "Snoop Datalink Types".
tldr.outcome: Future codes from 27 on are assigned First Come First Served, and unassigned codes 10-15 and 19-25 are reserved.

today: RFC 3827 is Informational and the metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: What Snoop Files Need
sections.content: RFC 1761 defines the snoop file format used to store captured network packets for tools that capture, display and interpret traffic. Its header has a Datalink Type field identifying the network's datalink type. This memo defines new values for that field and an IANA registry for future ones.
sections.plainLanguage: Each saved recording says what kind of cable it came from. This memo adds new kinds.

sections.title: New Datalink Types
sections.content: In addition to the codes in RFC 1761, the memo defines Fibre Channel as 16, ATM as 17, ATM Classical IP as 18 and IP over Infiniband as 26. The IP over Infiniband packet format is described in an external reference.
sections.plainLanguage: Four new kinds of cable get their own number.

sections.title: The IANA Registry
sections.content:
The new registry, Snoop Datalink Types, holds 32-bit (4 octet) values. It contains the earlier RFC 1761 values, from IEEE 802.3 at 0 through Other at 9 (including Ethernet at 4 and FDDI at 8), plus the four new ones.

New allocations from code 27 onward follow the First Come First Served policy. Codes up to 26 not defined by the document (10-15 and 19-25) are reserved.
sections.plainLanguage: There is now an official list of labels. New ones are handed out to whoever asks first, and some gaps are saved.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo says adding new datalink type codes to the existing file format poses no known security risks.
sections.plainLanguage: Adding more labels does not make anything less safe.

references.text: Callaghan, B. and R. Gilligan, "Snoop Version 2 Packet Capture File Format", RFC 1761, February 1995.
Narten, T. and H. Alvestrand, "Guidelines for Writing an IANA Considerations Section in RFCs", BCP 26, RFC 2434, October 1998.
